text:
Connor Bedard has 14 points in 12 games, and he called the 9-2 loss to Carolina "embarrassing," per theScore, after a players-only meeting. It was a sixth straight game without a win, and Chicago has won once in its last ten. The noise around him now is about help: headlines about Chicago's first-round picks and what they could buy.

His own numbers are sound. He's producing 3.45 points per 60 minutes, near the top of his talent range, and his goals match his chances almost exactly (5 on 5.3 expected). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 63% of his entries and getting to the dangerous ice at the 91st percentile.

The problem is what happens behind him. Chicago gets just 44% of the expected goals with him on at five on five. That's still four points better than the team without him, but Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season say opponents created a lot more with him on the ice, bottom 1% of forwards, while he played with the weakest teammates in the league. Watch the defensive numbers: that's the next step, and the roster isn't helping him take it.
headline: Bedard is fine. The Blackhawks are not
